name: 1612 Prairie Avenue: the brick stable on the alley, K12

function.note: The 1911 sheet draws the whole building crossed by one X, the key's sign for a stable (the T-1840 census: '2-storey brick stable (X) on the alley, drawn in two parts by a dashed partition'), and Robinson's 1886 plate 10 crosses the brick building it draws on the same ground, the atlas's stable. Carried to 1904 between the two, INFERRED; no source names a horse or a carriage on this lot.

research_note: T-1932 refines the district draft (T-2334) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit, the fifth coach house built from it after 1812's (T-2321), 1736's (T-2995), 1620's and 1616's (T-1932; 1616's stands against its south end). The sheet census (census row s20-1612-r1, trace s20fp-1612-b2) carries the building into 1904; the draft rules now skip that row. The kit is built in mirror image (`mirror`), its party wall at the south end against 1616's and its open gable, with the sheet's window mark, to the north. Robinson's 1886 plate draws a crossed brick stable about 7.1 m deep and 14.5 m along the alley here, the size of the 1911 building's alley part west of the sheet's dashed frame partition; the yard part beyond it is first seen in 1911. No picture of it is known. The reading is in docs/RESEARCH/k12-1612-goodman-stable-1932/README.md.

documented_range.note: STANDING IN 1904 rests on two maps either side of it. Robinson's 1886 plate 10 draws a brick stable, crossed, on the alley behind lot 8 (1612), about 7.1 m deep and 14.5 m along the alley (pink-density profiles on the committed plate raster, columns 339-359.5 and rows 1084-1126, at the plate's 0.346 m a pixel): the size, within the plate's line widths, of the 1911 building's alley part west of its dashed frame partition (7.87 by 15.23 m). The 1911 sheet draws that part and a second part to the east, 6.14 m more, behind the frame partition and under the same X and the same '2'. So the alley part stood from before 1886 through 1911, and the T-1840 census rules the whole building present in 1904 (present_as_mapped), as the district draft did; the east part is first seen in 1911 and may postdate 1904, which nothing read here settles. FROM: the record claims the 1904 target and no earlier day. TO: the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

position.symbolic_location: 1612 S. Prairie Avenue, rear: on the alley, its south end against 1616's stable, parcel prairie_1612 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).
position.note: The middle of the building's alley (west) wall at grade, read off the committed sheet 20 raster (chicago/reference/prairie-avenue/sanborn-1911-and-robinson-1886/sanborn_1911_vol3_sheet_20.jpg) at pixel (2229, 1967): the alley wall's line by median darkness profile over rows 1850-2090 (peak at column 2229, the column 1616's reading found below it), halfway between the north wall line (row 1817) and the south one (row 2117; 1616's own north wall line is at 2124.5, 0.38 m beyond it), each the peak of a median darkness profile over columns 2260-2480. Carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_20_gcps.json): local E 1333.689, N -2989.151. The bearing is the parcel's and the house's (goodman_house_1612_prairie, -0.578 degrees). The fit's own residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed; the draft stood the building inside a 13.5 by 14.5 m rectangle fitted to its trace.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; none reads a 1911 Sanborn sheet. This position is pixel (2229, 1967) of the committed sheet 20 raster carried through the similarity in data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_20_gcps.json (local_e = a*px + b*py + c, local_n = d*px + e*py + f) plus the datum origin, and the note carries the pixel and the result so the sum can be recomputed by hand.

footprint.note: About the middle of the alley wall, u east (into the lot) and v north. The sheet draws the building from the alley line (pixel column 2229) to its east wall line (2505) and from its north wall line (row 1817) to its south one (2117), each the peak of a median darkness profile: 276 by 300 pixels at the sheet's 0.050779 m a pixel, 14.015 m deep by 15.234 m along the alley. A dashed line, the key's frame partition, crosses it from north to south at column 2384, 7.87 m from the alley line; it is inside the building and not built. The district draft's fit found a 13.5 by 14.5 m rectangle inside the traced part.

stories.note: '2' on each part, either side of the frame partition: two storeys throughout.

construction.note: Drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick, with wall thicknesses lettered '12 8' (inches, the first storey's and the second's, as the key reads them) inside its north wall and again inside its south wall. Robinson's 1886 plate also colours the alley part pink, its brick.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the storeys, the brick and the sheet's two window marks is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-1612-stable-1932. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, walls '12 8', a stable's X over the whole, a dashed frame partition 7.87 m from the alley, and two of the key's window marks: on the alley wall about 8.38 m from the north wall line with a dot for each storey (openings in both storeys there), and on the north wall about 9.29 m from the alley line with one dot (an opening in one storey, built in the first as 1620's one-dot mark is). It draws no fire-wall sign on this building. The kit is built in MIRROR IMAGE (`mirror`): its party wall stands at the south end, against 1616's party wall 0.38 m away (the sheet draws the two wall lines apart, rows 2117 and 2124.5), and its open gable at the north end, which faces 1608's open rear yard and carries the sheet's one-dot mark. Every opening's s counts from the party wall's inner face (the alley and yard walls' s from the south end and the north end respectively, as the kit lays them; the gable's from the alley face). The alley wall carries a stable sash and a loft sash over it where its mark stands, a man door with a loft sash over it toward the south end, and the kit's carriage bay (3.0 m clear) toward the north end with the loft hatch over it; the yard wall a door onto the workyard at its middle between two stable sash and two loft sash; the north gable one stable sash where the sheet's mark stands and nothing over it. The south end's party wall rises the kit's 0.45 m above the roof, where the sheet draws no fire-wall sign: the kit has no second open gable, and the south end is the one that stands hidden against 1616's taller party wall. A gable roof with its ridge along the alley at 30 degrees (1736's, 1812's and 1616's deep-stable pitch) over the 14.02 m span, about 4.0 m from eave to ridge; whether the yard part, first seen in 1911, ran under one roof with the alley part or under its own is not read, and one roof is built. No external stair, ramp, lean-to, wing or ventilator: the sheet draws none. Not built: the frame partition (inside), the sheet's solid dot near the south-east corner (the key's vertical steam boiler; the kit has no stack and the sheet draws none) and a small cross near the south end of the alley wall that the key does not explain. The workyard is paved from the yard door to the house's rear wing, 13.0 m east of the yard wall.

coach_house.note: The building's dimensions are the footprint's (inferred, above); its openings, roof and workyard are the kit's, laid out for this lot with the sheet's two window marks where it puts them, and RECONSTRUCTED. See the value's own note for each choice and what bounds it.
